thread:
SRE Bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for /v1/generate (streaming) across prod-us-west-2 — p99=2.8s, baseline 0.6s. creating incident channel. severity=P1
Alex W: I’m on it. seeing many streaming stalls and partial chunks not arriving. p95 up to 300ms, p99 2.8s like bot says.
Priya R: paging now. @Mateo can you check KV cache metrics? suspect heavy eviction rate.
Mateo C: pulling KV metrics... eviction_count spiked at 10:13:22 UTC, eviction_rate ~120/s for the last 5m. fragmentation_ratio jumped to 0.68.
Jin L: logs show a bunch of long-prefix requests from a single client org at 10:12:58 — large context sizes (>= 64k tokens) causing huge prefill writes.
Oncall Ops: customer-impact check: CS reports 3 major customers seeing streaming stalls and some websocket disconnects. ticket IDs: CS-8371, CS-8373.
Darren M: any recent deploys? Deploy Bot: @Darren M deployed model-routing change at 10:05 UTC to prefer v2-small on low-tier; rollout 40%. no rollback.
Alex W: that rollout shouldn't cause global KV pressure, but combined with large prefixes it could. Mateo, do prefill vs decode durations show imbalance?
Mateo C: yes. prefill latency spiked to p99=1.2s while decode remained ~0.3s. suggests prefill writes are the hotspot and causing eviction churn.
Priya R: quick mitigations: 1) throttle prefill writes, 2) route streaming traffic to fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint, 3) temporary scale up of KV pool. rank them.
Alex W: prioritize routing fallback + scale-up. throttling prefill is riskier to change in prod without canary.
Jin L: I can push a routing override to send streaming requests to v1-compact in us-west-2 for the next 15m. will prepare a command.
Alex W: do it. Also open port-forward to control-plane to run cache diagnostic.
Deploy Bot: routing override applied by Jin L at 10:24 UTC: route /v1/generate streaming -> v1-compact (traffic cut ~55% in us-west-2).
Mateo C: scaling KV pool now: increasing node count +2 — API invoked. estimated 90s to be healthy. eviction rate falling already by 10%.
SRE Bot: NOTE: autoscaler activity recorded, nodes added: kv-node-22, kv-node-23.
Oncall Ops: update from CS: two customers report decreased stalls after 10:30 UTC, but one still seeing 10-20% streaming chunk delay.
Alex W: running quick heap/fragmentation check on a sampled KV instance: lots of small free blocks, high fragmentation, compaction not keeping up. compactor process shows high CPU and is OOM-killed occasionally.
Priya R: that explains eviction cascade: prefill writes allocate, compactor can't keep up → fragmentation → evictions → decode misses → more prefill attempts. vicious loop.
Darren M: can we temporarily increase compactor memory limit and restart compactor on 3 nodes? low risk.
Mateo C: doing controlled restart on kv-node-05,07,12 now. increasing memory to 4Gi for compactor container.
Jin L: also lowering prefill parallelism per request by envvar PRE_FILL_PARALLELISM=2 on serving runtime for us-west-2; applying to canary subset immediately.
Alex W: logs after routing + scale show p99 falling: 2.8 -> 1.1 -> 0.7s within 20m. streaming stall rate down ~70%.
Oncall Ops: incident update: severity remains P1 until p99 < 0.8s for 30m and no customer regressions.
Customer Success: flagged customers notified of mitigation steps, offer follow-up call.
Priya R: postmortem TODOs: 1) hard limit on per-request prefill size, 2) compactor autoscaling improvements, 3) circuit-breaker on large-prefix clients, 4) better routing policies for large context flows. assign owners?
Alex W: Priya owns circuit-breaker proposal, Mateo owns compactor/autoscale, Jin owner for routing playbooks. Darren to follow-up on deploy rollback policy. I'll start incident writeup.
SRE Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED -> p99 under threshold for 45m, streaming stall alerts cleared at 10:55 UTC. closing channel in 1h unless new regressions.
Alex W: thanks all. main takeaway: prefill-heavy traffic + KV fragmentation triggered eviction storm. followups scheduled. :thumbsup:
Priya R: adding action items to the ops board and scheduling a 1hr post-incident review tomorrow 16:00 UTC.
Mateo C: will attach KV diagnostic snapshots and sample heap dumps to the incident ticket.
Darren M: leaving final note: consider load-profiles for large-context customers and a paid-tier path with isolated KV pools.
Customer Success: customers marked as impacted and SLA credits flagged if needed.
Alex W: closing here — if anyone sees regressions, reopen thread or page.
